newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak cbank sees crown stable in near term - paper.
newsitem.headline: Slovak cbank sees crown stable in near term - paper.

text.p: A renewed attack on the Slovak crown is unlikely in the near future and the crown should be stable at current levels, National Bank of Slovakia vice-governor, Marian Jusko, was quoted as saying.

In an interview with Slovak business daily Narodna Obroda on Friday, Jusko said he thought it unlikely foreign investors would simply withdraw from Slovakia and said those who were betting on a devaluation would lose money.
"I don't expect this (another attack), taking the foreign commitment in the Slovak economy into account," Jusko told the paper.
"Those domestic and also foreign speculators who were betting, or even still consider betting on the quick devaluation of the crown, have posted significant losses," he added.

In an attempt to avoid the fate suffered by the Czech crown, which lost nearly 10 percent of its value after a sustained speculative assault, the Slovak central bank has squeezed liquidity on the interbank market and intervened directly to support the crown.
Juska said that despite the expense entailed in keeping interbank rates so high -- overnight rates are over 50 percent -- the central bank's recent measures were "very correct."

He added that the NBS had spent around five percent of the hard currency reserves of the entire Slovak banking sector in defending the crown. Total banking sector reserves were $5.1 billion as of May 28.

Despite his upbeat mood on the crown, Juska acknowledged that Slovakia's trade deficit remained a serious problem which would need to be resolved if the crown were to remain secure in the longer term.
Last month the statistical bureau said the country's trade deficit totalled 27.908 billion crowns for the January-April period, up from 21.498 billion for the same period in 1996.
